title: One national regulator for offshore petroleum safety and environment (NOPSEMA)
summary: From 1 January 2012 the offshore petroleum safety authority became NOPSEMA, which also took on environmental management and well integrity regulation in Commonwealth waters, so operators deal with one regulator for safety and environment plans.

instruments.title: Offshore Petroleum and Greenhouse Gas Storage Amendment (National Regulator) Act 2011

commenced.what: Schedule 2 (NOPSEMA) commenced in the principal Act

direction_rationale: In 2007 operators told the Productivity Commission that they submitted the same safety and environmental information at different times to different agencies under separate management plans.

verified.notes: Assent and the 1 January 2012 commencement of Schedule 2 from the Federal Register (the compilation of the principal Act that incorporates the amendment).

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Offshore safety, well integrity and environmental plans now go to one national regulator instead of several bodies, reducing duplicated submissions that operators had complained of.

marks.reason: One regulator for safety, well integrity and environmental plans reduces duplicate submissions.

assessment.confidence_note: The duplication was documented by the Productivity Commission in 2007; no later evaluation was found.
